parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, facility ban, or documented police/border targeting; same-sex conduct was decriminalised in 2012, so sexuality law is not a traveler exposure. Resident gains — no legal gender recognition, no general anti-discrimination statute, marriage limits — are not deducted per the traveler rule. Offsetting this, the dossier documents societal discrimination, taboo/stigma and community-level SOGIESC discrimination in a 2024 submission, with undated rape/assault reports, and no documented working visitor remedy. A 2017 analysis notes a passport/presentation mismatch could face an unspecified charge, but no enforcement is documented — an open question, not an established exposure. Historical police support for Pride and a freely operating LGBTI organisation (2013-2016) is positive but dated, and there is no documented trans-specific social acceptance, facility, or custody practice. This is elevated risk: no universal or organised targeting, but thin recourse and documented hostility.
